Index.about us main: We are a group of passionate students from PushQuantum e.V., a student initiative based in Munich. Our team is made up of a diverse group of physics and engineering students from the Technical University of Munich and Ludwig-Maximilians University, united by a shared enthusiasm for quantum science and technology.
Index.sub hello: Discover the amazing world of quantum physics with interactive courses and practical examples.
Index.difficulty description: Whether you're a beginner, intermediate, or advanced learner, we have content tailored to your level.
Index.Difficulty Elementary 2: Perfect for beginners with no prior knowledge of quantum concepts.
Index.Difficulty High School 2: Designed for students with basic understanding of physics and mathematics.
Index.Difficulty College 2: Advanced content for university students and professionals.

About Us.motivation subtitle: Bridging the gap between quantum science and society through education, innovation, and collaboration
About Us.s1 p1: Quantum technology is usually described in one of two registers: Headlines that promise a revolution without explaining things precisely, or publications written for specialists. Readers who are curious but not yet experts often find little between the two.
About Us.s1 p2: We seek to provide an engaging space for everyone to learn about quantum technology, regardless of their prior knowledge. Hence WiQi was built.
About Us.s1 p3: You can find a variety of quantum subjects — be it entanglement, decoherence or superconductivity — on three levels: an easy, a medium and a difficult version. These are not three separate texts but one explanation at three depths. You may begin at whichever level suits you the most, and move up as your understanding grows.
About Us.s1 p4: Alongside these encyclopedia-like entries, WiQi also collects write-ups of the Quantum Tuesdays (Quantendienstag) lecture series at the Deutsches Museum, and a short glossary of quantum terminology under Quantum Alphabet. All of it is available in German and English, and all of it is freely accessible.
About Us.s2 p1: WiQi was developed within <qtr>Quanten(t)räume</qtr>, as a “digital twin” of the project. Quanten(t)räume is a collaborative science-communication project funded by the <bmftr>Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space</bmftr>, running from December 2023 to November 2026.
About Us.s2 p2: The project proceeds from the conviction that second-generation quantum technologies should be discussed rather than merely announced. Its partners develop outreach formats that connect to one another: museum exhibits, advanced courses in school laboratories, teacher training, public lectures, and games. Three overarching goals run through all of these formats:
About Us.s2 goal1: Creating networked spaces, online and at several locations, in which the public can learn about quantum technology, exchange views with one another and with specialists, and think through possible applications together.
About Us.s2 goal2: Supporting early-career researchers and vocational education through science-communication training, advanced courses at the PhotonLab school laboratory, school seminars and teacher training.
About Us.s2 goal3: Prompting dialogue between the general public and experts, and enabling both sides to learn from each other, to give researchers a concrete picture of how quantum technology is seen by the public.
About Us.s2 p3: Hence the purpose is not only to attract talent to the field, but to ensure that quantum technologies develop in step with what the public actually understands and wants.
About Us.s2 p4: WiQi is a written and lasting layer of this work, and aims to demystify quantum technology for the general public.
About Us.s3 p1: Quanten(t)räume is coordinated by the <dm>Deutsches Museum</dm> and carried out together with:
About Us.s3 partner1: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics (MPQ) — PhotonLab
About Us.s3 partner2: Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research (ISI)
About Us.s3 p2: <mcqst>MCQST</mcqst>, <iqm>IQM</iqm> and the <mqv>Munich Quantum Valley</mqv> are associated partners.
About Us.s4 p1: PushQuantum e.V. is a student initiative based in Munich, formed by students from the Technical University of Munich and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität.
About Us.s4 p2: This initiative is community-driven: our members lead the projects they care about, supported by the network around them. Our work rests on three pillars: community, professional development, and outreach. WiQi belongs to the third, under the Quanten(t)räume project.
About Us.s4 p3: We believe that quantum science and technology have the potential to revolutionize our future. Thus, we are committed to equipping society with the knowledge and tools to prepare for and actively participate in this movement.
